text:
Alex G.: Heads-up — during the mid-day load test I’m seeing p99 blow up from ~220ms to ~1.2s. Correlated with KV miss rate jumping and a bunch of kernel fallback logs. Anyone tracking KV-eviction storms? :thinking:
Maya R.: saw that too, added a trace: https://internal-traces/trace/1840007890 :eyes: kv.miss_rate spikes to 18% at 1k concurrent users
Liam T.: quick profile: selector falls back to `generic_gemm` for ~long sequence paths once memory layout changes after an eviction. excerpt from node log:
```
[2026-07-14T14:18:12Z] kernel_selector: preferred=optim_gemm(seq=128) -> fallback=generic_gemm reason=kv_cache_layout_mismatch
[2026-07-14T14:18:12Z] kv_cache: evict_count=3489 current_size=0.78GB
```
perf-bot: Regression alert: p99 increased 5.4x on canary group during 14:15-14:25 window. Linked runs: run/1840007890/compare
Rachel S.: ran a microbatch sweep earlier this morning. numbers were: window=30ms -> p95 210ms p99 1.15s; window=80ms -> p95 260ms p99 420ms. So larger window reduces tail but hurts median for small single-turn requests.
Alex G.: that matches my observations. We’re trading off p95 vs p99. For interactive endpoints small requests care about median; for batchy workloads tail matters.
Maya R.: thought: the root seems to be KV churn evicting hot prefixes under high concurrency. If kernel_selector sees fragmented KV layout it disables some fused kernels -> cost spike. Two axes to try: reduce eviction churn (reserve per-model hotset) OR make kernel selection resilient to fragmented layouts.
Liam T.: agree. Proposed quick experiments:
- soft kv reservoir: reserve ~128MB per-model and track recency to avoid mass evictions during spikes
- adaptive microbatcher: increase window when tail signal (p99 delta) rises, shrink for median-sensitive traffic
- promote optimistic kernel with a fallback fast-path that avoids full generic path when possible
Rachel S.: quick numbers from local sim with soft reservoir=128MB + window=50ms: p95 235ms p99 480ms, kv.miss_rate down from 18% to 6%. promising.
Alex G.: can we do a canary that changes only the kv-reservoir and keeps batch window unchanged? That isolates effects.
Maya R.: yep. Also adding a small prefetch for the top-3 recent KV keys per session reduced first-token latency on misses in sim. snippet: 
```
prefetch_recent_kv = true
prefetch_count = 3
```
Liam T.: operational notes: need a rollback/circuit-breaker if reservoir causes memory pressure on hosts. plan: canary 1% traffic -> monitor host mem, kv_eviction_rate, p99. If mem > 85% rollback.
Rachel S.: and add a kernel-selector flag so we can flip kernel priority during the canary without deploy rollback. Just disable the optimistic kernel if we see regression.
ci-bot: Canary deployment scheduled: canary/kv-reservoir-128MB -> start in 10m, %traffic=1. Health checks: p95,p99,host_mem,k v_eviction_rate.
Alex G.: thanks. After canary we should run a focused load test that replicates our 1k concurrent spike and capture full flamegraphs. If fallback still occurs we'll need to dig into the selector heuristics. :thumbsup:
Maya R.: opening a short runbook and a PR with config flags. Assigning follow-ups: @Liam T. kernel selector logs, @Rachel S. perf run configs, @Alex G. canary watch.
Liam T.: noted, will attach flamegraphs to the runbook.
Rachel S.: I’ll also add a dashboard alert that triggers on kv.miss_rate > 8% and p99 delta > 200ms.
perf-bot: Test matrix queued: reservoir=[64,128,256]MB x window=[30,50,80]ms x kernel_flag=[on,off]. Expected runtime ~3h.
Alex G.: nice. Keep it tight and we'll reconvene after the canary results.
